---
title: "A From-Scratch CNN on the Kaggle Digit Recognizer Dataset"
description: "A compact case study training a small CNN from scratch on MNIST: careful evaluation beyond accuracy, published via Quarto."
---

## Overview

This project is a compact case study in convolutional neural networks, built on the classic Kaggle **Digit Recognizer** (MNIST) dataset.

MNIST is well known and trivially solved, so this is not a benchmark-chasing exercise. The goal is a small CNN trained from scratch (no pretrained weights), built and evaluated carefully — with attention to what kind of mistakes the model makes, not just its final accuracy.

---

## Problem Statement

Given a 28x28 grayscale image of a handwritten digit, the system must:

1. Normalize and prepare the raw pixel data.
2. Train a small convolutional network from scratch.
3. Evaluate it with a confusion matrix and a side-by-side inspection of correct and misclassified examples, not accuracy alone.

---

## Methodology

* Load the Kaggle CSV pixel data, reshape to 28x28 images, normalize to `[0, 1]`.
* Random train/validation split.
* A small CNN: two convolutional blocks (conv -> ReLU -> max pool), followed by a dropout-regularized dense head.
* Train with Adam and cross-entropy loss for a small number of epochs.
* Evaluate: accuracy, confusion matrix, and a side-by-side look at correct vs. misclassified digits.

---

## Dataset

The project uses the **Digit Recognizer** dataset from Kaggle.

* Competition: [https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/digit-recognizer](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/digit-recognizer)

28x28 grayscale handwritten digit images (0-9), provided as flattened pixel values in CSV form.

## Project Structure

The repository is organized as follows:

```text
kaggle-digit-recognizer/
│
├── README.md                                    # Project overview and usage instructions.
├── pyproject.toml                                # Package + dependency spec (pip install -e .).
├── index.qmd                                     # Landing page for the Quarto website.
├── _quarto.yml                                   # Quarto website configuration.
├── LICENSE                                       # Project license.
│
├── scripts/
│   └── publish.sh                                # Executes the notebook and publishes the site to GitHub Pages.
│
├── notebooks/
│   └── digit_recognizer.ipynb                    # Single notebook: data prep, training, evaluation.
│
├── src/
│   └── digitrecognizer/
│       ├── dataset.py                            # Loading, reshaping, normalization.
│       ├── model.py                              # Small CNN definition.
│       ├── train.py                              # Training loop.
│       └── evaluate.py                           # Metrics, confusion matrix.
│
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                                      # Original Kaggle CSV files.
│   └── processed/                                # Intermediate artifacts, if any.
│
├── outputs/
│   ├── checkpoints/                               # Saved model weights.
│   └── figures/                                   # Training curves, confusion matrix, correct/misclassified prediction examples.
│
├── tests/
│   └── test_model.py
│
└── _site/
    └── ...                                        # Website generated by Quarto (gitignored - published via scripts/publish.sh, not committed).
```

The site is published to GitHub Pages by running `scripts/publish.sh`, which executes the notebook and then runs `quarto publish gh-pages`.

## Status

Complete: trained and evaluated against the Kaggle data (the CNN reaches ~99% validation accuracy), and published to GitHub Pages.
